docs: ADR-0006 (Proposed) — skill distribution and installation

Drafted in response to retrospective gap #6 (skills are exported
constants today, not installable into agent environments). Frames the
question generally so it scales to multiple skills as Tier 2 lands
(Seven Principles, Meeting Practices, Peer Development).

Core decision: skills are installable artifacts distributed as npm
packages and installed via flyway-cli (which currently is a stub —
this gives it its first real job). Three subcommands proposed:
flyway skill list / install / uninstall. Target resolution infers
from environment markers (.claude/skills/, etc.) with explicit
--target override.

Scope for v0.1 deliberately narrow: only flyway-agent is registered;
only SKILL.md is written (no scripts/references/assets subdirs until a
real skill ships them); update + content-hash safety deferred.

Future skills adopt flyway- namespace prefix as convention. CLI
imports content from skill packages, never hardcodes — adding a skill
is publish package + register in CLI.

Status: Proposed. Implementation follows acceptance.

docs(walkthroughs): 3-party retrospective-cadence trial of Tier 1 protocol

End-to-end test of flyway 0.1.0 (SHA 02e1bfa) with three independent
subagents reasoning from distinct murmuration contexts plus one
facilitator subagent, on a realistic scenario: three peer murmurations
collaborating on a year-long joint paper needing to agree on
retrospective cadence.

The protocol carried the full arc tension → independent acknowledgements
with divergent suggestions → facilitator integration into a
requirements-stage proposal → consent round (2 accept + 1 object) →
objection integration into a refinement → predicted consent on refinement.

What worked:
- Three subagents produced genuinely independent, distinct positions
  (none pre-emptively softened)
- §IV.1.6 objection-vs-concern test classified correctly under load
- Facilitator integration produced a novel two-layer structure none of
  the three suggested individually
- Source C raised a textbook §IV.1.6 objection (premise + conclusion +
  proposed resolution); §IV.1.7 integration cycle resolved it cleanly
- 12 substantive concerns recorded across the accept responses
- Agreement schema carried the integrated output without forcing

Gaps surfaced and filed:
  #1 flyway_propose is 2-party only (singular peerDid)
  #2 Tension → proposal promotion has no first-class linkage
  #3 concerns_to_record not first-class on flyway_respond
  #4 Facilitator role not first-class in the protocol
  #5 Multi-party consent flow unspecified
  #6 Structured requirements field on flyway_propose
  #7 Operable triggers not structured in agreement schema
  #8 No validation of stage transitions

Walkthroughs are tied to git SHA + protocol version so progress over
time is auditable. docs/walkthroughs/README.md indexes them.

feat(core): flyway_propose stages from S3 §IV.1.9–1.10 (Tier 1 #4 — Tier 1 complete)

S3 Proposal Forming (§IV.1.10) is a 7-step pattern for developing
proposals through stages instead of in a single shot. ADR-0005 committed
to capturing this with an optional stage field on flyway_propose
(driver / requirements / draft / refinement). final is added as the
default to preserve single-shot proposals.

Mapping from S3's 7 steps to flyway's 4 stages + default:
  driver       = §IV.1.10 step 1 (Consent to Purpose)
  requirements = §IV.1.10 steps 2-4 (Questions, Info Gathering, Generative Qs)
  draft        = §IV.1.10 steps 5-7 (Collect Ideas, Choose Tuners, Tuners Design)
  refinement   = post-objection revision (§IV.1.7 Resolve Objections cycle)
  final        = ready for consent decision (default)

Two new fields on flyway_propose:
- stage (optional enum) — defaults to 'final'
- previousStageId (optional string) — links a refinement back to its draft
  so the staging chain is traceable without inferring from issue order

Responses to non-final stages are signals about the proposal's evolution,
not consent decisions — the instructions name this explicitly so peers
don't mistake "no objections to this draft as a draft" for consent.

New section in protocol instructions explains the stages and when each
applies; routine matters can still go straight to final, novel work
benefits from the early stages.

Five new tests pin the stage enum, optional-ness, previousStageId field,
and the §IV.1.9-1.10 citation. ADR-0005 Tier 1 row updated; this closes
Tier 1 — all four sub-tasks resolved. 40/40 tests passing; MCP smoke
test confirms stage field served correctly over stdio.
